steps.text: Combine zucchini and onion in a large bowl.
Mix flour, cornmeal, salt, pepper, and garlic powder together in a small bowl until well combined.

Pour flour mixture over zucchini mixture; cover the bowl and shake until vegetables are evenly coated. Let the coated vegetables sit until the flour mixture becomes slightly moist and clings to the vegetables, about 30 minutes.

Heat oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Fry vegetables in batches in the hot oil until golden brown and crisp, turning as needed to cook evenly. Drain briefly on paper towels before serving.

raw_recipe.headline: Fried Zucchini
raw_recipe.description: This fried zucchini and squash with onion features a seasoned cornmeal-flour breading that cooks up golden brown and crisp for a savory appetizer.
raw_recipe.name: Fried Zucchini

review.reviewBody: This is an excellent recipie. Even my son who does'nt like zuchinni said so. I did increase the salt in it. Also I used one zuchinni and one yellow squash. Easy, fast and delicious. Thanks.

I am astounded at how simple this method is, and how wonderfully the end result was! I can honestly only rate the method, because I used 1 cup of Zatarain's frying mix instead of the dry ingredients. The zucchini and onions came out crispy and stayed crispy. For those who ended up with soggy results, here are a couple of tips. Keep shaking that bowl of zucchini while the 30 minutes passes. I also shook it between batches, and I waited longer than 30 minutes. Second, make sure your oil temperature stays right around 350. I will use this method from now on! Thanks for the recipe, Jon!

This was good and fairly easy. I liked the idea of using Italian seasoned bread crumbs and parm, in addition to the cornmeal. Next time, I might use less cornmeal. I like to salt my zucchini after slicing and layer in a bowl with paper towels in between, prior to mixing with the breading mixture. I do this whenever using zucchini. Helps get rid of some of the excess moisture.

I made it in the airfryer. Oiled the zucchini a bit dumped on the dry batter and it fried up in about 20 min on 400. Nice and crispy, oh and I sprayed it with a little Pam spray when I stopped it midway and moved stuff around. This was great

I thought this turned out pretty darn good. I used onion powder instead of onions. I seasoned the veggies directly and heavily seasoned the flour too. I used a mix of almond flour/ coconut flour and shredded Parmesan instead of regular flour ( Keto) I fried some of them in olive oil and some in lard. I think I preferred the olive oil. I followed the recipe and fried some as directed then I also did a flour/egg wash/ flour to some of them. I equally enjoyed both. The egg wash veggies made a larger fritter. I made some roumalade sauce to dip. Very yummy.

Do this simchannas way and its a 5 star. Dip in eggwash than flour than eggwash again. Garlic salt and pepper and fry. Plus make sure to pat with paper towels. Now thats how mom useda make!!*mmmm* P.S. These are also very addicting and So far my all time favorite way to use up my zucchini.

Although it didn't really look like the picture this was a nice fried zucchini recipe. It wasn't what I was expecting - there isn't really a "batter" that happens. However, once I played around with it a little it worked pretty well. The zucchini inside is nice and moist and the outside just crispy enough without feeling really greasy. A couple of tips - definitely let it sit for at LEAST half an hour. I tossed and mixed it around with my fingers a few times during that too. Then as you're taking the zucchini pieces out, dredge them in the loose powder at the bottom. The moistness of the zucchini will cling to the powder and you'll get better coating that way. I ran out of time and couldn't make them all so I stuck it in the fridge. It was there for two days and then I made the rest and they came out just as well, if not better!

This recipe is GENIUS! I have fried zucchini for years, trying all kinds of batters. This is by far the easiest and best. The zucchini are much crispier than any I've ever cooked. My husband liked them, too. I couldn't understand how this would work - with no liquid at all. But it did! I followed the recipe exactly, except for adding a little sugar and Cajun seasoning. I also did all the prep in a gallon baggie, so it ended with a toss in the trash can, instead of washing multiple dishes. After 30 minutes exactly, I fried them. The medium heat didn't do it for me. The first batch took way too long to cook and weren't getting brown. So I raised it just a little, to 7/10. Loved the onion combination. I'm SOLD! Thank you!

hmm... seemed to be missing something. I ended up with a few burned pieces before making some modifications:
Dip moistened zucchini in flour/cornmeal, then in an egg wash, then in breadcrumbs. Pan fry for about 1-2 minutes each side. Delish with ranch dressing...

I have been frying zucchini for years, and I have to say this is the best recipe I have ever tried! My whole family loved it. I added garlic salt and seasoned salt for added flavor and I simply tossed everything into a Ziplock bag for 30 minutes. The zucchini had a nice crisp coating and did not soak up a lot of oil unlike a lot of fried zucchini recipes. I can't wait to make more tomorrow night!

Super tasty! I have never used cornstarch in the flour, It is amazing how well everything stays together in the oil. My zucchinis were a little dry so I dipped them in egg before the cornstarch mixture so a batter formed and I added a little extra salt and pepper once cooled .
Delicious! Loved the way the zucchini slices ‘weeped’ Causing the coating to stick. It worked like a charm. I did add a teaspoon of Cajun seasoning to zip up the flavor.
Loved it. I made 1 zucchini & 1 squash. Will make again.

Nice, it was a hit. Make sure you use freshly cut and juicy young zucchini so the water beading up on the cut surfaces causes the breading to adhere. If you don't have that, maybe do a milk or egg soak to get the breading to stay on. If zucchini is large (a common problem when gardeners let them go too long), then peel it and cut into even sized spears instead of discs.

I will definitely make this again. I didn't make any changes and was very surprised how well the batter stuck to the zucchini without using an egg as I have always done in the past. I will try making this again using other types of squash.
Tried many fried zucchini recipes. This is absolutely the best. I was hard to not eat it before it ever got to the table! I only made one tiny change - added some parmesan before serving!
I don't get the reviews with egg in them , I don't see any egg in the original recipe? I make this as the recipe suggests and it turns out really good!
